items.headline: Learn the 4Ts: Rayleigh mother shares her daughter's intensive care ordeal so parents spot type 1 diabetes sooner
items.summary: Mandy was told to prepare for the worst when Zara, then 13, reached Southend Hospital. Months of warning signs had gone unnoticed.
body: A Rayleigh mother who was told to prepare for the worst at her daughter's hospital bedside is urging every parent to learn the 4Ts of type 1 diabetes: toilet, thirsty, tired and thinner. Mandy has told Zara's story through NHS Essex in the hope that other families catch the signs before a child becomes dangerously ill.

Zara had felt worn out on a family trip in August 2025. Back home she was sick and struggling to breathe, and at Southend Hospital she was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), a life-threatening condition that develops when the body runs short of insulin. Mandy says staff got a defibrillator ready in case her heart stopped and told her to call the family in. Looking back, the signs had crept up for months: stomach and back pains, constant tiredness and thirst, frequent trips to the toilet and dizzy spells. Mandy says she had never heard of the 4Ts and likens what followed to "a catastrophic plane crash rather than a managed emergency landing".

Zara spent a week in hospital and now lives like any other teenager, using a glucose monitor and an insulin pump. Dr Deepa Shanmugasundaram, a GP and clinical lead at NHS Essex, said symptoms can develop quickly. Mandy has since started a monthly meet-up in Rayleigh where families of children with type 1 diabetes can share experiences and tips.
points: Child with the signs? Get a same-day check through your GP or NHS 111
Severe stomach pain, rapid breathing, vomiting or confusion: call 999 or go to A&E
Family meet-ups: second weekend of each month, 11.30am, Manzano Lounge, High Street, Rayleigh
